_note: The latency of the carrier before he decides again, in ticks (10 ticks = 1 s; IDEA-DESIGN-011, R.1-latency; ADR-044 §6, R.1-relation). latency = base_ticks * (1 + (1 - decision_making) * decision_bias) * (1 + crowd_weight * crowding + threat_weight * nearest_threat). Rescaled 2026-11-12 (OI-97): base_ticks was 1334, derived to reproduce the prototype's mean wait between actions (1/0.0005 = 2000 ticks, the density of the old die), not the time a footballer takes to choose; measured latencies were 142-394 s and the match stood still. With base_ticks 7 a strong decider in space chooses in about 0.7 s, a weak decider under pressure in about 2-3 s, which is the order of magnitude of a real match. crowd_weight and threat_weight are the weights of the two scene terms. A third term, plausible_options, is tracked as OI-96. decision_bias 0.0 means decision_making does not change the pace; 1.0 means a weak decider (0.0) waits twice as long as a strong one (1.0).
_source: Order of magnitude of a footballer's decision time on the ball (about 0.5-3 s), from observation of real matches; not calibrated (L3). The form is a model choice (multiplicative biases, no die, ADR-035); scene terms added by R.1-relation (ADR-044 §6, 2026-11-10). Previous base_ticks 1334 derived from action_probability 0.0005 (CHANGELOG-SIM entry 18), superseded by this rescaling.
